The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T03:02:03Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T03:02:27Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came 6 minutes 3 seconds {detection_gap} after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
Broken from 2026-11-11T02:55:00Z {began} (the onset). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T03:04:19Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 9 minutes 19 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 1 minute 55 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T03:04:19Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 30.0% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 39.0% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 29.1% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9833333333333333% {series_before} before it began, 30.05% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 39% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: at least 6,142.30 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T03:02:24Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T03:02:30Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T03:02:30Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T03:02:38Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 03:02:03 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T03:02:43Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T03:02:44Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:55 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T03:02:45Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T03:02:46Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 11 02:56 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T03:02:47Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T9.2} production changes
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T03:02:47Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T03:02:48Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 37 {T11.2} minutes 3 {T11.3} seconds before 03:02:03 {T11.4}
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T03:02:48Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 133 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T03:02:50Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T03:02:50Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T03:02:50Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 03:02:50 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T03:02:55Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T03:02:56Z {T17.1} Argus: Refused to act on C1 - the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T03:02:56Z {T18.1} Argus: Moved the incident to FIXING - no explanation left to try - no action was taken, and the evidence offers nothing further
  - [T19] 2026-11-11T03:04:19Z {T19.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/540
  - [T20] 2026-11-11T03:04:19Z {T20.1} Argus: Moved the incident to ESCALATED - a draft pull request is open at https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/540

Changes to production it read:
  - Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 30 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 30 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 02:25–02:54 {G7e5d.4}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 6 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 23 {Gad41.2} minutes, 02:25–02:47 {Gad41.3}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 43 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 37 {G46bc.2} minutes, 02:26–03:02 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 32 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 37 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 02:26–03:02 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 34.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 02:56 {Gbac1.7}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 174 {G971b.1} / on 26 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 02:55 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 8 {G5309.2} minutes, 02:55–03:02 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 7 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 7 {Gce95.3} minutes, 02:56–03:02 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The monthly-spend-feature flag was switched from off to on at about 2026-11-11T02:55:00Z {C1.1}. This enabled the spend summary path, which raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and fails roughly 30% {C1.2} of account page requests. No deployment, config change or rollout split is recorded. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.3}, never tried: the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person]

Actions it took:
  - none

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by `len(bought_this_month)`, the number of the account's purchases that have `in_current_month` set. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has no such purchases, so the function raises ZeroDivisionError. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py calls that kind of shopper "the ordinary case", and its own helper builds one. `render_spend_summary` calls this function whenever `use_monthly_summary` is true and `use_typical_spend` is false. So turning on monthly-spend-feature made every idle shopper's page in that slice fail, which is the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 that the investigation found. Turning the flag off hid the error but didn't remove it.
      
      The fix: if nothing was bought this month, the function now returns 0 {F1.1} (nothing spent per item this month) instead of dividing. The return type stays int, so `render_spend_summary` and its callers in src/io_shop/account_page.py get the same kind of value as before. Shoppers who did buy this month take the same arithmetic as before.
      
      What's unchanged: the lifetime `average_spend_per_item` still raises for an account with no purchases at all. The existing tests in test_spend_summary.py and test_account_page.py depend on that: they check that the error reaches the request boundary, and that the reported line contains `//`. That function sits above the one I changed, so its line numbers don't move. The edit adds no try/except, so other failures still propagate as before.
      
      The tests: two new tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py. One calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` for a shopper with past purchases but none this month and expects 0 {F1.2}. The other goes through `render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True)` for the same shopper and expects 0 {F1.3}. Against the current code, both would raise ZeroDivisionError at the division.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #540 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` (as long as `use_typical_spend` is false). That function divides the account's total for this month by the number of its purchases marked `in_current_month`. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has none, so the division is by zero and their account page request raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: A setting that adds a monthly spending summary to account pages came on, and nothing Argus read records who or what turned it on; the summary's code likely fails when it works out an average for shoppers who have bought before but bought nothing this month.
still_at_risk: While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers who had bought before but not this month, and the flag could be switched again without showing up in any change record Argus reads.
symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. That error first appears in the logs at the onset and nowhere before it. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: The monthly-spend-feature flag began evaluating on. Every evaluation logged during {G7e5d.4} was off. At {G971b.6} some evaluations were on, and the logs show it on during {Gce95.4}. The switch appears in no change record Argus read: the production change events returned {T9.2} changes, and the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus. What switched the flag is not in the record. No deploy or other change was recorded, so none could be ruled out by the service being measured healthy with it in place. (cites G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; T9, under "What Argus did, in order"; T15, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 4: Turning the flag on sent account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month down a code path that divides by their number of purchases this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: The switch of monthly-spend-feature to on was not recorded in the production change events or the flag provider's history, so Argus had no recorded change it could undo and refused to act on C1.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: Had the switch been recorded, Argus could have turned the flag back off during the response. That would have stopped the failing account pages instead of leaving the flag on for a person to deal with.
contributing_factors 2: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Once Argus left undoing the flag to a person, a paged on-call engineer could have turned the flag off and shortened the incident.
contributing_factors 3: No test was seen that exercised the flag-gated monthly summary for a shopper who has bought before but not this month before the flag was turned on. Code-Fix reports that the existing tests call this shopper the ordinary case and their own helper builds one.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would have raised ZeroDivisionError before the flag reached production, and the flag would not have been turned on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors 4: The flag went from on for part of traffic to on for all of it, and no guard was seen that held or reverted it while the account page error rate rose.
contributing_factors 4 had_it_been_otherwise: A rollout held at the first slice, or reverted on the rising error rate, would have limited the failures to a small share of shoppers or ended them soon after they began.
action_items 1: Turn monthly-spend-feature off for io-shop until the proposed fix is merged and deployed.
action_items 2: Find out how monthly-spend-feature was switched on without appearing in the flag provider's history or the production change events.
action_items 3: Make every flag change on io-shop go through the flag provider so it is recorded in the history Argus reads, and close any path that switches flags outside it.
action_items 4: Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page.
action_items 5: Require tests that run each flag-gated code path with its flag on, including shoppers with past purchases but none this month, before the flag can be enabled in production.
action_items 6: Make flag rollouts on io-shop stage through traffic slices, and pause or revert automatically when the error rate rises.
went_wrong 1: No mitigation was applied during the response: the flag was still on and account pages were still failing when the incident was escalated to a person.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
